building.title: Kenneth Myers Centre, University of Auckland
building.note: outline: traced from the LiDAR (building.outline_note), in the map's frame; chooses the crop box and the building's own points (frame.near_outline, measure and topview). campus_outline: building 820's outline from the main project's campus.json, kept for the record; the site replaces block 820 by its id, and topview measures the share of that block under the model.
building.outline_note: traced from the LiDAR's roofs and wall returns in the view frame of frame.expected (walls fitted to the returns: front z 16.2, porch front 14.8, east front 11.6, back -12.6, west x -16.7; the east wall from (21.4, 11.6) to (19.9, -12.6), skewed 3.5 deg as its parapet's returns run), taken to the map's frame. campus.json's outline (campus_outline) lies about 2 m north of the building's front and back (its front edge at z 11.8-12.7 against the LiDAR's 16.2; its back at -11.6 to -13.8 against -12.6) and adds a west tail (x -21.6 to -15, z -19 to -3) over the low lane beside the tower to the west and an east nub (x 21 to 27, z 7 to 13) over the low roofs to the east. Within 1.5 m of it the first data run took 94% of the building's roof returns, the mast's, and none of the tower's (no return above 40 m), but cut off the front 2 m of the street face (z 14.2 to 16.2 west of x 1.3) and its south-west corner; so the points are chosen by this ring, within 1.0 m of it. (The data stage's heightmap figure draws the map-frame outline without taking it to NZTM, so there it stands about 5 m off: most of that is the frame difference heightmap.py names.)

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6) within near_outline m of building 820's outline from campus.json (the first data run, before the outline was traced from the LiDAR: building.outline_note): centre = mean x/y of points higher than tower_above m: the front range's and the two roof blocks' tops at 10.0-10.2 m and the mast; axis = the bearing of most of the walls seen from above (axis_from walls), the one of the two square to each other nearest the principal axis of the points from min_above to spine_below m within spine_radius m, pointing west-south-west (street_side east); toStreet = the axis turned 90 deg toward street_side: south-south-east, to Shortland Street. With the traced ring and near_outline 1.0 the centre would be 0.73 m from this one (x -0.41, z +0.61 in this frame): the model, the cameras and the placement keep frame.expected.

streetview.pano_ids_note: the Google panorama of 2026-04 (32 m) that the sight-line test over the LiDAR finds seeing the Kenneth Myers Centre's east, south-east and south faces whole
streetview.camera_fixes_note: 0Rjk's camera, fitted to its wide view's own edges against the LiDAR (round 1, 2026-10-28). The panorama records a tilt of 95.89 (5.89 deg off level) and a roll of -2.41 deg, which tools/streetview_collect.py does not apply when it cuts the views: in them the verticals lean (a downpipe on the east part at column 930 by about 5 deg, its top to the right), and the east part's coping, level in the LiDAR (p90 8.02-8.07 m), runs nearly level across the photograph (rows 317 to 300 over columns 837-1558) where a level camera draws it rising 86 px. Fifteen points of the east part and the porch: the five pinnacles at the LiDAR's x (their returns above 8.5 m), each at its coping (8.05 m) and at its tip (one unknown height for all, fitted: 9.34 m), the porch's coping at x 4.0 (8.86 m), and the columns of its four spires at the LiDAR's two blocks. With its views cut turned back by 4.53 deg (the fifth number) and drawn from x 16.26, z 29.53 (1.12 m from the recorded camera), 5.68 deg lower and 0.83 deg right of the cut's aim, they fit at rms 9.5 px (|r| p50 6.7; the largest, 22.3, at the first pinnacle's tip, which stands higher than the rest, 9.93 m); a turn of 4.0 or 5.0 deg fits at 9.9 and 9.5 px. The panorama's own tilt and roll give, 240 deg round from its heading where these views look, a pitch of -5.0 or -0.8 deg and a turn of 3.9 or 6.3 deg (as the signs of its tilt and roll are read): the fit's sizes. Cut level, the downpipe stands upright (column 932 from row 420 to 520). Through this camera the east part's merlons stand at 7.96 m (the LiDAR's 8.05), its pinnacles within 0.2 m of the LiDAR's x, the porch's coping at 8.74 m (8.86) and the door's centre at x 3.91 (4.0 between the blocks). The recorded camera and the cut's aim leave the fifteen points at rms 80.6 px; the round's first fix, [18.35, 28.94, -3.54, 7.08] (no turn; fitted by the run stopped at 13:44, its points not kept), at 32.8 px; the best fix of four numbers over them and the west end's three at 28.8. The west part does not agree: the photograph's west part (columns 330-550) is a face with a level coping, its left end a corner with a pinnacle at column 330, which this camera puts at x -8.3 on the west part's face (z 16.21) with the coping at 7.0 m and four pinnacles 3.1 m apart, where the LiDAR's west part runs to x -16.7 with its top at 10.3-10.9 m (its tall front over x -15.5 to -9.5 only, its top set back to z 14.2-14.7 east of there); a level camera puts that corner at x -16.7 but its coping sloping from 11.0 to 8.8 m. Whether the panorama is stitched unevenly there (its copyright reads 'From the Owner, Photo by: Google') or the building has changed since the LiDAR of 2024 (the photograph shows a building site before it) is open; the model keeps the LiDAR's west part, and nothing on it is measured through this camera.

light.note: the viewer's light for this building (pipeline/viewer/main.js; the address still wins): the Clock Tower's sun, low in the north-east and so behind this south-south-east street face, which stands in open shade as the photographs' bright, cloudy April day shows it (soft light, no shadow cast on it). Exposure 2.2 with the kit's brickBrown (round 1): the building's luma median drawn 129, 118 and 115 against the photographs' 138, 121 and 122 in the wide, upper and door views (the views cut level); at 2.0, before they were cut level, 115/119/111 against 128/121/122. Round 0 (exposure 1.0 and the kit's red brick) drew 66 against 121-126.
